notes.A: The STATION lettering dominates, while the high angle hides the entrances beneath their awnings.
notes.B: The two signs tie the frontage together, but the near awning fills the foreground.
notes.C: The open doorway and receding lamps give the station depth, but the awnings interrupt the lettering.
notes.D: The wide view establishes the forecourt, but the station is pushed to the right edge.
notes.E: Both entrances and the facing facade frame the forecourt, but the station interior disappears into darkness.
notes.F: The narrow passage shows the tall facades, but the station frontage is barely visible.
notes.G: The lamps lead across the forecourt toward the station, whose nearest entrance is cropped.
notes.H: The open entrance has depth, but the foreground lamp and low awning dominate.

station_front.best: E shows both station entrances, the lamplit forecourt, and the ornate building across the way in one readable view.
station_front.lacks: A recognizable station entrance. The timber-framed openings have little architectural presence, and the dark interior gives no hint of where passengers are headed.
station_front.fix: Rebuild the main entrance as a broad, lit station portal with the full Gravesend Station name over the opening.

blind_name.name: Lamp-lit cobblestone courtyard
blind_name.why: Streetlamps line a cobblestone square framed by tall brick and stone buildings.
blind_name.odd: The far end of the right passage is obscured by darkness.
